subject: general
question: Which of the following countries celebrated Poson Poya Honoring 2000 Years of Buddhism in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poson Poya** is a major religious and cultural festival celebrated by Buddhists in **Sri Lanka** to commemorate the arrival of **Buddhism** in the country.
 
• The festival takes place annually on the **Full Moon** day of **June**, which is known as **Poson** in the **Sinhala** calendar. In **June 2025**, the nation marks this significant milestone with island-wide celebrations.
 
• It commemorates the arrival of **Arahat Mahinda**, the son of the **Indian** **Emperor Ashoka**, who brought the teachings of the **Buddha** to **Sri Lanka** in the **3rd Century BC**.
 
• The historic introduction of **Buddhism** occurred at **Mihintale**, where **Arahat Mahinda** met and converted **King Devanampiyatissa**, the reigning monarch of the time.
 
• The celebrations in **June 2025** honor the enduring legacy of over **2000 years** of Buddhist tradition, which has fundamentally shaped the **culture**, **social structure**, and **governance** of **Sri Lanka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Significance**: 
 
 
• **Mihintale**, located near the ancient city of **Anuradhapura**, is regarded as the cradle of **Buddhism** in **Sri Lanka**. During **Poson Poya**, thousands of **pilgrims** climb the **1,840 steps** to reach the summit of the sacred mountain.
 
• **Anuradhapura**, a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, serves as the primary hub for religious observances, including **Sil** campaigns and meditation sessions.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Traditions**: 
 
 
• Devotees engage in **Amisa-puja** (offerings of food and flowers) and **Pratipatti-puja** (following the path of Dhamma). Many laypersons observe **Atthasila** (the eight precepts) while wearing **white** attire.
 
• A unique feature of the festival is the **Dansala**, where local communities provide **free food**, drinks, and snacks to **pilgrims** and travelers as an act of **generosity** (Dana).
 
• The streets are decorated with **Buddhist flags** and **illuminated lanterns**. Large structures called **Pandols** (Thoranas), depicting stories from the **Jataka tales** (previous lives of the Buddha), are erected with colorful electric lights.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: 
 
 
• Following the meeting at **Mihintale**, **Buddhism** became the **state religion** of **Sri Lanka**. This led to the establishment of the **Mahavihara** monastery and the flourishing of **Pali literature** and **Sinhalese architecture**.
 
• The **Government of Sri Lanka** typically declares a **Poson Week** to facilitate religious activities and ensures the protection of sacred sites during the influx of **pilgrims**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Vesak**: While **Vesak** (celebrated in **May**) commemorates the **birth**, **enlightenment**, and **passing away** (Parinirvana) of the **Buddha**, **Poson** is specific to the **Sri Lankan** context, celebrating the localized birth of the **Dhamma** on the island.
 
• **National Importance**: **Poson Poya** is a **Public Holiday** in **Sri Lanka**. In **2025**, special focus is placed on **interfaith harmony** and the **preservation of ancient monuments** that date back to the initial conversion period.
 
• **Modern Observance**: Modern celebrations often include **Poson Bhakthi Gee** (devotional songs) and processions (**Peraheras**) involving traditional **dancers** and **drummers**.
